note: Published spot heights against our products. Written and committed BEFORE any of our values at these points was looked at; not to be edited afterwards. The commit time is the authoritative time of writing.

source.citation: D. E. Smith et al. (2010), Initial observations from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA), Geophys. Res. Lett. 37, L18204, doi:10.1029/2010GL043751, section 7.1
source.what_it_says: a global LOLA grid at 1/16 degree (about 2 km); highest elevation 10.7834 km at 201.378 E, 5.401 N; lowest elevation -9.117 km at 187.5074 E, 70.360 S, in Antoniadi crater
source.datum: elevations relative to the 1737.4 km sphere, the LOLA convention also used by our products (stated as such in the LOLA GDR labels; the paper does not restate the datum in this sentence, so this is an assumption to be checked by the result)

method: for each product that covers the point: (a) our bilinear height at the stated coordinates; (b) the extreme (max or min as stated) of our heights on a 250 m grid within 5 km of the stated point, and its distance from the stated point. The published grid is from 2010 (less data, older orbits, 2 km cells), so the comparison is at the tens-of-metres level.
products: LDEM_16, LDEM_128 and any SLDEM2015 mosaic for both points; LDEM_60S_60M for the Antoniadi point (70.36 S lies inside its square)
